question: A 37-year-old man presents a picture of arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal of both hands and a right pleuritis. On examination, bilateral malar erythema was observed. Positive antinuclear antibodies are detected (titre 1/640), with native anti-DNA antibodies also positive; Anti-Sm negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?

options.opd: The picture will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

analysis: The clinical presentation of arthritis in the metacarpophalangeal joints, pleuritis, bilateral malar erythema, and positive antinuclear antibodies with native anti-DNA antibodies suggests a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The initial treatment for mild to moderate SLE, particularly with joint and skin involvement, often includes non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and antimalarials like hydroxychloroquine. These medications help manage symptoms and prevent disease flares. High-dose glucocorticoids or immunosuppressive agents like mycophenolate are typically reserved for more severe organ involvement.
